title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttnV2 with fused ops, rotary/rope fixes, KV-batching and scheduler optimizations
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We continue to push inference throughput and tail-latency improvements for production workloads. This change upgrades our attention kernels to a vetted FlashAttnV2 integration, adds fused QKV+ROPE/rotary ops, fixes a subtle rotary alignment bug, and introduces KV-batching and scheduler heuristics to improve GPU utilization for mixed-length workloads.

Summary of changes:
- Integrate FlashAttnV2 kernels with our runtime (CUDA/C++ bindings) and expose a runtime switch to prefer FlashAttnV2 when available.
- Implement fused QKV + ROPE application kernel to reduce memory traffic and kernel launch overhead for rotary embeddings.
- Fix rotary offset calculation for multi-head models where past_key_value lengths are not divisible by head dim chunk size. This resolved a small correctness regression observed in long context evals.
- Add continuous KV-batching support in the scheduler to aggregate KV write/read when requests share prefix tokens or compatible key shapes.
- Scheduler heuristics: prefer fused kernels for short/medium sequences, fall back to standard kernels for very long sequences where memory fragmentation becomes a concern.
- Add unit tests, microbenchmarks, and end-to-end perf harness updates.

Performance (representative):
- End-to-end decode throughput +28% on A100 for 2k-token chat workload (single-request decoding, batch size 1).
- p99 latency improved ~18% on mixed-length concurrent workloads (8 concurrent streams).
- Memory working set reduced ~12% due to fused ops and reduced temporary buffers.
- KV-batching increases amortized throughput by ~22% for high-prefix reuse workloads.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Runtime will auto-detect FlashAttnV2-compatible GPUs/driver stacks; behavior is gated behind runtime flag REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATNV2 and an instance-level config.
- Backward-compatible: when flag is off or GPU unsupported, we fall back to existing kernels.
- Added Canary rollout: we first enable on Dedicated clusters with lower SLO sensitivity, then gradually ramp to Hosted.

Testing and validation:
- Added kernel-level unit tests and integration tests in perf-canary that exercise long-context decoding and KV cache correctness.
- Added regression tests to catch rotary misalignments (reproduced previous failing example).
- CI: GPU integration tests run on kitchen infra. One flaky CI job (gpu-infer-e2e) was stabilized by increasing a buffer timeout and mocking noisy telemetry; tests re-ran and passed.

Related PRs/Work: ENG-8421 (kernel validation), ENG-8570 (scheduler heuristics), related prior attention upgrades: pr-61234, pr-67239, pr-70500.

Release notes: See release_notes field below for user-facing summary and migration notes.

perf(attention): fused QKV + ROPE CUDA kernel + host bindings

perf(scheduler): continuous KV-batching and prefix-aware heuristics
test: add kernel/unit tests and perf harness cases
ci: stabilize gpu-infer-e2e by increasing buffer timeout and retries
discussion: Jordan Lee (reviewer): Can you add a guard so models with nonstandard head dims don't hit the fused path? Response: Added runtime check that only enables fused kernel when head_dim % 8 == 0 and past_kv chunking matches. See rotary_utils.cc change.

Priya Nair (reviewer): What's the expected fallback behavior for very long sequences? Response: Scheduler heuristic will select the legacy kernel for sequences > 8k tokens; documented and gated via config.See continuous_batching.cc comments.
Samir Gupta (reviewer): Please add a short benchmark script for CI to prevent regressions. Response: Added perf-canary harness and an automated nightly job to run the microbenchmark.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed review comments, added tests and stabilization for flaky CI. Ready for merge after one more perf run.
Priya Nair: approved with comments resolved
release_notes: Users: we upgraded our default attention kernels to a FlashAttnV2-backed implementation which provides ~20-30% throughput improvements and lower p99s for many decoding workloads. This is opt-in via REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATNV2 and will be gradually rolled out. No API changes. Operators: ensure drivers and CUDA toolkit meet FlashAttnV2 minimums (notes in docs/release/notes/attention-flashattn.md). If you observe regressions, toggle the runtime flag to fall back to legacy kernels and open a support ticket referencing SUP-1291.
notes: Canary rollout started 2026-02-26 on Dedicated; full Hosted rollout completed 2026-03-01. Monitoring dashboards added to Redwood Console (per-model kernel selector metric and kernel-fallback counters).
